newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says 41 bids for three bank sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says 41 bids for three bank sell-offs.

text.p: Turkish deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Tuesday 41 bids were received in the sell-off tender of three state-owned banks, Etibank, Anadolubank and Denizbank, which closed on Monday.

"We started to get satisfactory results in privatisation and revenues from sell-offs will begin to come to the Treasury from the New Year," she told reporters after a meeting with senior economy officials.
Nine bids were received for Etibank, 15 for Denizbank and 17 for Denizbank. The tender was opened on November 18 and closed on Monday.
Privatisation officials said another 12 bids were received in the tender for the privatisation of two tourist facilities and two properties of land owned by state tourism firm Turban.
Bids were sought in dollar terms in all of the tenders.
State minister Ufuk Soylemez said after the same meeting that bids received in high numbers and values for the tenders "showed confidence in the country's privatisation."
Turkey's privatisation agency OIB targets revenues of some $5 billion from 1997 sell-offs, although only some $3 billion has been raised since the programme began in 1986.
